title: An escaped high surrogate directly followed by an escaped low surrogate is one character
notes: Production [60] ns-esc-16-bit escapes a 16-bit Unicode character, and YAML 1.2 aims to be a superset of JSON (section 1). RFC 8259 section 7 writes a character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane as a UTF-16 surrogate pair of two \u escapes, so the kit reads a high surrogate escape followed directly by a low surrogate escape as the one character the pair encodes (U+1F600 here). The YAML text alone does not say this, so the case carries the convention tag. It covers lower-case and upper-case hexadecimal digits and a pair between other characters. A surrogate that is not half of such a pair is refused (see the mismatched and lone cases).

provenance.reference: A decoder that refused the two escapes of a surrogate pair, or turned each half into a replacement character, so a JSON string with a character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane could not be read.
